disagreements.topic: Alternate-function labels for pins 12, 35, 38, 40 in the Fritzing part
disagreements.says_a: pin 12 GPIO 18 (PCM CLK), pin 35 GPIO 19 (PCM FS), pin 38 GPIO 20 (PCM DIN), pin 40 GPIO 21 (PCM DOUT)
disagreements.says_b: pin 12 BCM 18 (PWM0), pin 35 BCM 19 (MISO), pin 38 BCM 20 (MOSI), pin 40 BCM 21 (SCLK)
disagreements.resolution: Not a conflict on the GPIO numbers: both agree on BCM 18, 19, 20, 21. Fritzing names a different alternate function (PWM0 and SPI1). For the I2S amplifier wiring use the pinout.xyz PCM names. The Fritzing descriptions also misspell Ground as 'Gound' on pins 14, 20, 25.

disagreements.topic: Camera cable orientation wording in the day-1 bench notes
disagreements.says_a: insert with the contacts facing the board's contacts
disagreements.says_b: insert the cable with the metallic contacts facing away from the flap
disagreements.resolution: Same physical result on the Zero (flap on top, contacts down). Prefer the official wording on the page.

disagreements.says_a: Camera Module 3 family part numbers SC0872, SC0873, SC0874, SC0875 (no SC1224)
disagreements.resolution: Not resolved from an official Raspberry Pi page. DigiKey's product record 17278644 is reached by URLs carrying both SC0874 and SC1224, which suggests SC1224 is a newer ordering code for the same Wide module (inference). Identify the board by the silkscreen 'Camera Module 3 Wide', which matches the photo.
Not relevant to wiring; recorded only. The photo is unaffected.

disagreements.says_a: All models of Raspberry Pi Zero require a Raspberry Pi Zero camera cable; the standard camera cable does not fit
disagreements.says_b: The Standard - Mini camera cable fits the 22-way FPC connector on Raspberry Pi 5 and all Raspberry Pi Zero models
disagreements.resolution: Consistent: both describe a 15-to-22-pin cable. SC1892 is a valid Pi Zero W camera cable. The Camera Module 3 brief adds that early Pi Zero boards (before the camera connector was added) cannot take a camera at all; the Pi Zero W has the connector.

disagreements.says_a: Revision history: as of June 13, 2024 the terminal block is pre-soldered; only the optional header needs soldering.
disagreements.says_b: Assembly page still tells you to place and solder the 3.5 mm terminal block yourself if you want it.
disagreements.resolution: Product page is newer; the current shop photos (3006-04, 3006-07, 3006-08) and the dossier photo show the block already soldered. The Learn Pinouts lead photo is the older board without the block.

disagreements.says_a: Class D controller able to run from 2.7 V to 5.5 VDC.
disagreements.says_b: You can provide 2.5 V up to 5.5 V.
disagreements.resolution: The board back silkscreen in shop photo 3006-06 reads 'Vin: 2.5~5.5V', matching the Learn guide. Irrelevant for this robot because Vin comes from the Pi 5 V rail, inside both ranges.

disagreements.says_a: 3.2 W into 4 ohm at 5 V, 10% THD.
disagreements.says_b: 5 V into 4 ohm at 10% THD: 3 W max.
disagreements.resolution: Both agree on 1.8 W into 8 ohm at 5 V, which is the case for this robot's 8 ohm speaker.

disagreements.says_a: Page 1 photo shows a speaker with twisted red/black leads ending in a small white 2-pin plug
disagreements.says_b: CMS-30204-18SP: Mounting Style Solder Pads; alternate view shows two bare pads and no wires
disagreements.resolution: The datasheet covers the whole CMS-30204-18X series and its cover photo is not the SP part (the L200 drawing shows stripped ends, not a plug either). The ordered SP part has bare pads, matching the product page photo used here.

disagreements.topic: Speaker wiring in the day-1 bench notes
disagreements.says_a: Block 5: 'Speaker wires into the green terminal block' and asks for the speaker wire length.
disagreements.says_b: CMS-30204-18SP has solder pads (Mounting Style: Solder Pads); no wires are fitted.
disagreements.resolution: The ordered speaker has no wires. Two wires must be soldered to its pads (a one-time helper job like the amplifier header), or the wire-lead variant CMS-30204-18L200 is needed for a no-solder bench. The day-1 note needs this correction.

disagreements.topic: Maximum current the board asks for
disagreements.says_a: Uses the 'HUSB328 PDL003A E-Marker variant' which 'can request 5A power'; up to 20 V at 5 A (100 W).
disagreements.says_b: ISet jumper selects 1.25 A when closed (default) and 3.25 A when cut; the HUSB238 datasheet ISET table also tops out at 3.25 A.
disagreements.resolution: Unresolved by Adafruit's documents. The product page also says you get 'as much current as the adapter will provide'. Measure the actual current limit on the 20 V setup under load before relying on more than the board's requested current. 'HUSB328' on the product page is a typo for HUSB238 (chip marking and silkscreen say HUSB238).

disagreements.topic: Voltage choices on the DIP switch
disagreements.source_a: Parent task brief for this dossier (2026-10-10)
disagreements.says_b: 1x6 DIP switch: 5V, 9V, 12V, 15V, 18V, 20V. If none of the switches are ON, the highest voltage the USB PD supply offers is selected, which could be up to 20 V.
disagreements.resolution: There are six positions including 18 V. Safety consequence for the day-1 5 V test: exactly the 5V switch must be ON; all switches OFF is not 'off', it asks for up to 20 V.

disagreements.says_a: Schematic sheet 3 marks J8 and J9 "B3B-EH-A, DNP" (do not populate).
disagreements.says_b: 4 DYNAMIXEL ports are ready for TTL DYNAMIXEL.
disagreements.resolution: The product photo shows all four ports fitted (J11, J9, J8, J10). The e-Manual matches the photo.

disagreements.topic: Header type of the two edge ports
disagreements.says_a: J10 and J11 are "B3B-EH-A, DIP, R/A".
disagreements.says_b: In JST EH naming, B3B-EH is top entry and S3B-EH is side entry.
disagreements.resolution: The photo shows J10 and J11 as side-entry (right-angle) headers and J8 and J9 as top-entry. All four take the same JST EHR-03 plug, so wiring is unaffected.

disagreements.source_a: Parent task brief for this dossier (2026-10-10)
disagreements.says_b: JP1 positions are silkscreened VIN(DXL) and +5V.
disagreements.resolution: Use the board labels: VIN(DXL) for terminal-block power, +5V for USB (or the VIN header pin) power.

disagreements.topic: USB-only servo power in the day-1 bench notes
disagreements.says_a: Block 4: 'For one or two servos the USB port is enough (it has a 500 mA fuse)', then 'Move the OpenRB power jumper to VIN(DXL)' for the 5991 supply.
disagreements.says_b: Schematic: USB VBUS reaches only the +5V side of JP1; with the cap on VIN(DXL) USB does not power the board.
disagreements.resolution: Not a contradiction, but the note leaves the USB-only step's jumper position implicit: it must be +5V (the cap sits on +5V in the product photo). Move it to VIN(DXL) only when the terminal block is wired. The VIN(DXL) behaviour with USB only is read from the schematic and not bench-tested.

disagreements.says_a: Baud Rate(8) table includes value 7 = 4.5 Mbps (specification row still says 9,600 bps to 4 Mbps).
disagreements.says_b: Baud Rate(8) table stops at value 6 = 4 Mbps.
disagreements.resolution: Not visible on a photo. Irrelevant for bring-up: the default is 57,600 bps and the OpenRB-150 supports up to 1 Mbps.

disagreements.says_a: All DigiKey rows: purchase.order_placed=false (r3 snapshot of 2026-09-13). ROBOTIS controller and servo rows: merchant confirmed, received_quantity 0.
disagreements.says_b: DigiKey order 101587695 placed 2026-09-13, all 15 lines received (user confirmed 2026-09-29). OpenRB-150 and XL330 servos are on the bench today.
disagreements.resolution: The receipt record states it supersedes the BOM's order_placed=false for those 15 items. The ROBOTIS receipt is not recorded anywhere in the procurement folder; bom.json was left unmodified (read-only).
